x: Its meaning has already been explained in his saying: “Ha Meem. By the clear Book.”
And the clear Book.
And His saying: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. God Almighty swore by this book, that He sent it down during a blessed night.
The interpreters of the Qur’an differed regarding that night, which night of the year it was.
Some of them said: It is the Night of Decree.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, meaning the Night of Decree. The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was sent down six nights before Ramadan, the Psalms were sent down sixteen nights before Ramadan, the Gospel was sent down eighteen nights before Ramadan, and the Criterion was sent down twenty-four nights before Ramadan.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On a blessed night
, he said: It is the Night of Decree.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn.” He said: That night is the Night of Decree. God sent down this Qur’an from the Mother of the Book on the Night of Decree, then He sent it down to the prophets during the nights and days, and on other than the Night of Decree.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban. The correct statement about this is the statement of those who said: It refers to the Night of Decree, because God Almighty has informed us that this is the case, as He, the Most High, said: Indeed, We were to warn. We created this Book that We sent down on the blessed night, so that Our punishment would befall those among them who disbelieved and did not turn to Our Oneness and the singularity of divinity for Us.
And His statement:
h
In it every wise matter is decided

The people of interpretation differed regarding this night in which every wise matter is decided, similar to their difference regarding the blessed night. This is because the ha in His statement: In it refers back to the blessed night.
Some of them said: It is the Night of Decree, in which the affairs of the entire year are decided: who dies, who is born, who is honored, who is humiliated, and all the other affairs of the year.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said:
m: I was with Al-Hasan, and a man said to him: O Abu Saeed, is the Night of Decree in every Ramadan? He said: Yes, by God, it is in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is decided, in which God decrees every term, hope, and provision until its like.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said:
m: A man said to Al-Hasan while I was listening: Tell me about the Night of Decree, is it in every Ramadan? He said: Yes, by God, besides whom there is no god, it is in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is decreed, and God decrees every term, creation, and provision until its like.

c: Yunus told me, he said Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Abdul Hamid bin Salim said, on the authority of Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, he said: It is said that the Angel of Death copies the death of whoever dies on the Night of Decree to the same night, and that is because God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night and He said: Therein is decreed every precise matter. He said: So you will find a man marrying women and planting crops while his name is among the dead.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Therein is distinguished every wise matter

, he said: The matter of the year to the year is what it was of creation, sustenance, life span, calamity, or something like this. He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, who said: It was said: Wait for the judgment in the month of Ramadan.

c: Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Saeed bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Therein every wise matter is decreed
, he said: The affairs of the year are managed on the Night of Decree.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Therein is decreed every matter of wisdom
, he said: On the Night of Decree every matter that will happen from year to year: life and death, all livelihoods and calamities are decreed on it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night the Night of Decree in which every precise matter is distinguished. We used to say that in it the matter of one year is distinguished from the next.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It is the Night of Decree, in which whatever happens from one year to the next is decreed. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated from Mansur, who said: I asked Mujahid, saying: What do you think of the supplication of one of us, saying: O God, if my name is among the happy ones, then make it among them, and if it is among the wretched ones, then erase it from them and make him among the happy ones? He said: Good! Then I met him a year or more later and asked him about this supplication. He said: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn. * On that night is made distinct every matter of wisdom.” He said: On the Night of Decree, He decrees whatever provision or calamity will occur in the year, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the decree of happiness and wretchedness, it is fixed and cannot be changed.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah and Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Al-Hasan bin Ismail Al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty, Therein is made distinct every matter of wisdom, he said: On the night of the middle of Sha’ban, the matter of the year is decided, the living are copied from the dead, and the pilgrims are written down, and no one is added to them, and no one is subtracted from them.

c: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil ibn Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Akhns, he said:
m: “The Messenger of
b.via: Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Akhns

x: And His saying: “
h
A command from Us
. Indeed, We were sending messengers.” God Almighty says: On this blessed night, every wise matter is decreed,
h
a command from Us
. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement: Amrana.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is accusative because We sent it down as a command and a mercy in the state of Alif Laa ʿanzal We have sent it down as a command and a mercy.”
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It means that He separates every command into a division and a command.
He said: And likewise his saying:
h
A mercy from your Lord

. He said: It is permissible for mercy to be made accusative by the occurrence of messengers upon it, so mercy was made for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: Indeed, We were messengers means, the Most High said: Indeed, We were sending Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Our servants as
h
a mercy from your Lord

, O Muhammad. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing means: Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted be He, is the All-Hearing of what these polytheists say regarding what We have sent down of Our Book, and what We have sent of Our Messengers to them, and other than that of their speech and the speech of others. He is the All-Knowing of what their hearts contain, and other than that of their affairs and the affairs of others.
The reciters differed in their reading of His statement,
h
Lord of the heavens and the earth

. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as <Lord of the heavens>in the nominative case, following the i’rab of al-Samee’ al-Aleem. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Mecca read it as Lord of the heavens is a lowering in response to the Lord in His Almighty’s saying, A mercy from your Lord. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whoever recites them is correct. What is meant by his saying:
h
Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them is that God Almighty says

, He who sent down this book, O Muhammad, to you, and sent you to these polytheists as a mercy from your Lord, the Owner of the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them of all things. And His statement:
h
If you are certain
means:
h
If you are certain
of the truth of what I have told you, that your Lord is the
h
Lord of the heavens and the earth

, then what I have told you is that God is the One who has these attributes, and that this Qur’an is His revelation, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is His Messenger, is the absolute truth, so be certain of it as you are certain of what you are certain of of the truths of things other than Him.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Lord of the heavens and the earth.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as <Lord of the heavens>in the nominative case, following the i’rab of al-Samee’ al-Aleem.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Mecca read it as Lord of the heavens is a lowering in response to the Lord in His Almighty’s saying, A mercy from your Lord.
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whoever recites them is correct.

x: And His statement: There is no god but Him means: You people have no god but the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so do not worship other than Him, for worship is not appropriate for anyone other than Him, nor is it appropriate for anything other than Him. He gives life and causes death, meaning: He is the One who gives life to whomever He wills, and causes death to whatever He wills of what was alive. And His statement:
h
Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old

means: He is your Master and the Master of those of your forefathers who came before you. He says: So this one whose description is like this is the Lord, so worship Him instead of your gods who are unable to harm or benefit.

And His statement: Rather, they are in doubt, playing. God Almighty says that they are not certain of the truth of what is said to them and what they are told of this report. He is rebuking the polytheists of Quraysh with that, but they are in doubt about it, so they are playing with their doubt about what they are told of it.

God Almighty means by His saying: Then wait, so wait, O Muhammad, for these polytheists from your people who are in doubt and playing. It is an active verb, from the root word raqabah, meaning if you wait for him and guard him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So wait: meaning, wait. And His statement:
h
On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke

x: The people of interpretation differed about this which God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to await, and informed him that the sky would bring forth a visible al-Dukhan 44:what day it would be, and when it would be, and about the meaning of the smoke that was mentioned in this place.

Some of them said: That was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, against the Quraysh to take them with years like the years of Joseph, so they were afflicted with famine. They said: What was meant by the smoke was what would afflict them at that time in their eyes from the intensity of the hunger and the darkness like the appearance of smoke.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Isa bin Uthman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me, he said: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: We entered the mosque, and there was a man telling his companions stories, and he said:
h
The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke

. Do you know what that smoke is? That is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, and it will take away the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, and it will cause the believers to suffer from something similar to a cold. He said: So we went to Ibn Masʿud and mentioned that to him, and he was lying down. He was startled, so he sat up and said: God, the Almighty, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, nor am I of the pretenders.” [p. 86] It is part of knowledge for a man to say, when he does not know, “God knows best. I will tell you about that. When the Quraysh delayed converting to Islam and resisted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he called upon them to have years like the years of Joseph. They were afflicted with hardship and hunger until they ate bones and dead meat, and they raised their eyes to the sky but saw nothing but smoke. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: “
h
The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke

, * Enveloping the people. This is a painful punishment.” They said: “Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.” God, the Most High, said: “Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little. Indeed, you will return. * The Day We will strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take revenge.” (al-Dukhan 44:15-16) He said: So they returned on the day of Badr, and He took revenge. God is from them.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said: Malik bin Sa’ir told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: There was a man in the mosque reminding the people, so he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Isa, on the authority of Yahya bin Isa, except that he said: So he took revenge on the day of Badr, so it was the greatest blow. Ibn Humayd and Amr ibn al-Humayd narrated:

c: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim ibn Subayh, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: We were sitting with Abdullah ibn Masʿud and he was lying down among us. A man came to him and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, there is a storyteller at the gates of Kindah, who tells stories and claims that the Sign of the Smoke will come and take the breath away of the disbelievers, and that it will affect the believers like a cold. Abdullah got up and sat down, angry, and said: O people, fear God. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: God knows best. Amr said: It is more beneficial for one of you to say about what he does not know: God knows best. And it does not matter to one of you to say about what he does not know: I do not know. God the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: ‘I do not ask of you for this any reward, nor am I of the pretenders.’” When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the people turning away, he said: O God, seven days like the seven days of Joseph. Then a famine seized them that consumed everything, until they ate skins, dead bodies, and carcasses. One of them looked at the sky and saw smoke from hunger. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb came to him and said: O Muhammad, you have come to command obedience and to maintain kinship ties, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them. God the Almighty said: Then await the Day So await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.... until His saying: Indeed, you will return. He said: Then He removed from them “the Day We shall strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take revenge.” So the strike was the Day of Badr, and the verse of the Romans and the verse of the smoke, and the strike and the binding had passed.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: Abdullah said:
m: Five have passed: Smoke, Al-Lizam, Al-Batsha, Al-Qamar, and Al-Rum.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, who said:
m: I witnessed a funeral in which Zayd bin Ali was present, and he began to narrate on that day, and he said: The smoke will come before the Day of Resurrection, and it will cause a cold in the nose of the believer, and it will cause the ears of the unbeliever. I said: May God have mercy on you, our companion Abdullah had said something other than this. He said: The smoke has already passed, and he recited this verse: “Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful torment.” He said: The people were afflicted with such hardship that a man could see smoke between him and the sky. That is what he said: Then await. And Abdullah recited it like this until he said: Believers. He said: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little. (17:8) I said to Zayd: So they returned, and God brought Badr back to them. That is what he said: And if you return, We will return. (17:8) So that was the day of Badr. He said: So he accepted, by God. Asim said: A man responded to him, and Zaid, may God have mercy on him, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There will come to you narrators, so whatever agrees with the Qur’an, take it, and whatever is not like that, leave it.’”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he said:
m: The great blow was on the day of Badr, and the smoke had passed.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, who said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Aaliyah say: The smoke has passed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: The smoke continued for years and affected them.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: I was told that Ibn Masoud used to say: The smoke has passed, there were years like the years of Joseph.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke
, he said: drought and the withholding of rain from the infidels of Quraysh, until His saying: Indeed, we are believers.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke
. He said: Ibn Masoud used to say: The smoke has passed, and there were years like the years of Joseph. “It will cover the people. This is a painful torment.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke
, the matter of the smoke has already passed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: On the day when we will strike with the greatest strike, he said: On the day of Badr.

x: Others said: The smoke is a sign of God’s signs, sent to His servants before the Hour comes. It enters the ears of the disbelievers and affects the believers like a cold. They said: It has not yet come, but it will come.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Jami’, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Baylaman, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Smoke comes out and affects the believer like a cold, and it enters the ears of the disbeliever and the hypocrite, until it becomes like a roasted head.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, who said:
m: I went to Ibn Abbas one day and he said: I did not sleep last night until morning. I said: Why? He said: They said the comet appeared, and I was afraid that smoke might have come down, so I did not sleep until morning.

c: Muhammad bin Buzaie’ told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awf, who said: Al-Hasan said:
m: The smoke remains as one of the signs. When the smoke comes, the unbeliever will blow until it comes out of every one of his ears, and the believer will be seized with a cold.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Uthman told us,
m: meaning Ibn Al-Haytham, who said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, in a similar manner.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said:
m: Smoke will stir up the people. As for the believer, it will take hold of him like a cold. As for the disbeliever, it will stir up the smoke until it comes out of every nook and cranny of his. He said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: The similitude of the earth on that Day will be like that of a house in which a fire has been lit and in which there is no shortage.
Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah narrated to me, he said:

evidence.text: He said: The smoke has already passed, and he recited this verse: “Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people.
And Abdullah recited it like this until he said: Believers.

x: Their sight is overwhelmed by the effort that has befallen them. This is a painful torment.

Meaning that they say because of the distress and effort that has befallen them: This is a painful torment. It means that the word they say has been omitted from the statement, so that the listeners can know its meaning without mentioning it.

And His saying: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us means that the unbelievers who are afflicted with that hardship supplicate to their Lord by asking Him to remove that hardship from them, and they say: If You remove it, we will believe in You and worship You without any other deity besides You, as He, the Most High, said about them: “Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.”

God Almighty says: How can these polytheists remember after the calamity has befallen them, when they have turned away from Our Messenger when he came to them, not remembering what is recited to them from Our Book, nor taking heed from what he admonishes them with from Our arguments, and saying: He is only a madman who learned this speech. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement:
h
How will they be reminded
? the people of interpretation said.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
How will they be reminded
? He said:
h
How will they be reminded

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, How can they be reminded? after this calamity has occurred.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: How can these polytheists remember after the calamity has befallen them, when they have turned away from Our Messenger when he came to them, not remembering what is recited to them from Our Book, nor taking heed from what he admonishes them with from Our arguments, and saying: He is only a madman who learned this speech.

x: And similar to what we also said in his statement:
h
Then they turned away from him and said
, ‘A madman’s teacher,’ the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
Then they turned away from him and said
, ‘A madman’s teacher.’ He said: They turned away from Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and said, A madman’s teacher.

x: And His statement: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while. Indeed,
h
you will return

." God Almighty says to these polytheists about whom He informed that they seek help from Him from the descending smoke and the torment that befell them due to hardship, and He informed that they pledged to Him that if He removed the punishment from them, they would believe. Indeed, We will remove the punishment means the harm that befell them due to the fertility that We create for them. "For a little while. Indeed,
h
you will return
." He says: You polytheists, if I remove from you the harm that is upon you, you will not fulfill what you promise and pledge to your Lord of faith, but
h
you will return
to your misguidance and error, and you were not before He removed from you. Qatada said: It means:
h
You will return
to God’s punishment.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us
m: this, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on his authority. As for those who said that what is meant by His statement, On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, is the smoke itself, then they said in this passage: What is meant by the torment of which He said, Indeed, We will remove the punishment, is the smoke.

x: Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little, meaning the smoke.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little, he said: He did, He removed the smoke when it was. His saying:
h
You will return
. He said: He uncovered them and they returned.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
You will return
to the punishment of God.

x: God the Most High says: “O polytheists, if I remove from you the torment that has descended upon you and the harm that has befallen you, and then you return to your disbelief and break the covenant that you made with your Lord, I will take revenge on you on the Day when I will strike you with My greatest punishment in this world and destroy you.” And God removed the punishment from them, and they returned, so He, the Most High, struck them with His greatest punishment in this world and destroyed them by killing them with the sword.
The interpreters differed about the great punishment.
Some of them said: It is God’s punishment of the polytheists of Quraysh on the day of Badr.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he said:
m: The great blow: the day of Badr.

m: On the day when we strike with the greatest strike, he said: On the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
The Day We shall strike with the greatest strike
, he said: The Day of Badr.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, he said:
m: I heard Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding this verse,
h
The Day We strike with the greatest strike
, he said: The Day of Badr.

The Day We strike with the greatest strike

m: I said: What is the Greatest Blow? He said: The Day of Resurrection. I said: Abdullah used to say: The Day of Badr. He said: It reached me that he was asked after that and he said: The Day of Badr.

m: On the day of Badr.

The Day We strike with the greatest strike

m: regarding His statement:
h
The Day We strike with the greatest strike

It was mentioned that he said that:

m: Ibn Masoud said: The great blow was on the Day of Badr, and I say: It is on the Day of Resurrection.

m: Ikrimah passed by me, so I asked him about the great slap. He said: The Day of Resurrection. I said: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud used to say: The Day of Badr.
