m: The Day of Badr.
b.via: Someone who asked him after that

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Day We strike with the greatest strike

, Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan: It is the Day of Resurrection. We have previously explained the correctness of this, and the reason for which we chose to say what we chose to say about it.

x: And His statement:
h
And We certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh

means, God Almighty said: And We certainly tested and tried, O Muhammad, before the polytheists of your people, an example of these being the people of Pharaoh from among the Copts. And there came to them a noble messenger means: And there came to them a messenger from Us whom We sent to them, and he is Moses, son of Imran, may God’s prayers be upon him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh
, and there came to them a noble messenger, meaning Moses.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
A noble Messenger

, he said: Moses, peace be upon him. God Almighty described him as being noble because he was noble to Him and held a high position with Him. It is possible that He described him thus because he was noble and central among his people.

x: And His statement:
h
That you deliver to me the servants of God

, God Almighty says: And there came to the people of Pharaoh a messenger from God, who was honored by him, saying: Delivere me. The meaning of deliver is: Delivere me, so send with me and follow me. It is similar to His statement:
h
Send with us the Children of Israel
r
(Ash-Shu’ara’: 17)
So in His statement:
h
That you deliver to me
, there is an accusative, and the servants of God is an accusative with His statement: Delivere.

Some people interpreted it as: Delivere me the servants of God. So, according to this interpretation, the servants of God is an accusative as a vocative. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that they should be brought to me, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger, saying, ‘Give me the servants of God. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.’” He said: He says: Follow me to what I call you to of the truth.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
That you bring to me the servants of God
, he said: Send the Children of Israel with me.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
That you bring to me the servants of God
. He said: The Children of Israel.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
That you deliver to me the servants of God
, meaning the Children of Israel. He said to Pharaoh: Why are you holding back these people, a free people whom you have taken as slaves? Let them go.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
That you deliver to me the servants of God
, he said: He says: Send the servants of God with me, meaning the Children of Israel, and he recited: Then
h
send with us the Children of Israel
and do not torment them
r
(Ta-Ha: 47)
. He said: That is His statement:
h
That you deliver to me the servants of God

, he said: Return them to us. And His saying: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger means: I am to you, O people, a messenger from God who has sent me to you. His punishment will not overtake you because of your disbelief in Him. Trustworthy means: Trustworthy in His revelation and His message that He promised me to you.

x: God Almighty says: And there came to them a noble Messenger, [saying], Come to me, servants of God, and do not exalt yourselves above God. What he meant by his saying:
h
That you do not exalt yourselves above God is that you do not transgress and rebel against your Lord

, so that you disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, and thus go against His command. Indeed, I come to you with clear authority. He says: I come to you with proof of the truth of what I am calling you to, and evidence of its correctness, clear to whoever contemplates and ponders it that it is my proof of the correctness of what I am saying to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And do not exalt yourselves over God
: meaning do not seek to transgress against God. Indeed, I come to you with clear authority: meaning with a clear excuse.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: in a similar manner.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And do not exalt yourselves over God
means: Do not fabricate lies about God.

x: And His saying:
h
And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord
, lest you stone me. He says: And I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, and I have sought protection in Him from you, lest you stone me.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of the stoning from which the Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, sought refuge with his Lord.
Some of them said: It is verbal abuse.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from being stoned by you
, he said: He means stoning the speech.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Uthman bin Omar bin Faris told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from being stoned by you
, he said: Stoning means by word.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord
lest you stone me. He said: That you say he is a magician.

x: Others said: Rather, it is stoning.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord
from being stoned: meaning that you are stoned.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That you stone me. He said: That you stone me with stones.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying that you stone is that you kill me. The first of the opinions on this matter is what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the words, which is that Moses, peace be upon him, sought refuge with God from being stoned by Pharaoh and his people. Stoning may be a verbal statement or an action with the hand. The correct view is: Moses sought refuge with his Lord from every meaning of their stoning, which would cause harm and distress to the one being stoned, whether it be verbal abuse or stoning with the hand.
And His statement:
h
And if you do not believe in me

, then leave me. God Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:And if you, O people, do not believe in what I have brought you from my Lord, then leave me. He says: Leave me alone, without being stoned by tongue or hand.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if you do not believe in me
, then leave me alone: meaning, leave me alone.

x: God Almighty says: So Moses called upon his Lord when they denied him and did not believe in him, and did not bring the servants of God to him, and intended to kill him, because these, meaning Pharaoh and his people, are a criminal people, meaning: that they are polytheists and disbelievers in God.
And His statement:
h
So travel by night with My servants

. There is an omission in the speech that is sufficient in its indication of what was mentioned, which is: So his Lord answered him by saying to him: So travel by night, since the matter is thus, with My servants, and they are the Children of Israel. The meaning of the speech is:
h
So travel by night with My servants

who believed in you and believed in you and followed you, not those among them who disbelieved in you and refused to accept the advice you brought them, and those who were of this nature on that day were the Children of Israel. And He said:
h
So travel by night with My servants
, because the meaning of that is: Travel with them at night before morning. His saying:
h
You will be pursued
means: Pharaoh and his Copts will pursue you if you leave their country and their land in your footsteps.
And His statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease

means: If you and your companions cross the sea, leave it calm as it was when you entered it. It was said that God, the Exalted, said this to Moses after he crossed the sea with the Children of Israel. Since that was the case, then there is an omission in the statement, which is: So Moses traveled with My servants by night, and crossed the sea with them. So We said to him after he crossed it, and he wanted to return the sea to its condition before it split: Leave it at ease.
It was mentioned that God Almighty said to Moses, peace be upon him, this statement after he crossed the sea with his people:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: So he called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, these are a criminal people,’ until he reached Indeed,
h
they are a drowned army

. He said: When the last of the Children of Israel left, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to strike the sea with his staff so that it would return to what it was, for fear that the people of Pharaoh would overtake them, but it was said to him, Leave the sea alone, for
h
they are a drowned army

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: When he had crossed the sea, he turned to strike the sea with his staff so that it would reunite, and he was afraid that Pharaoh and his soldiers would follow him, so he was told: Leave the sea alone as it is, for
h
they are a drowned army

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of rahwa.
Some of them said: It means: Leave it as it was.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease
means: in a straight line.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “And leave the sea in tranquility. Indeed, they are a drowned host.” He said: Temptation means that you leave it as it was, for they will not be saved from behind it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of his father,
m: that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about the statement of God, “And leave the sea in peace,” he said: A path.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: Leave it easy.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: his saying:
h
And leave the sea at ease
, he said: Easy.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease
. He said: It is said: At ease means a plain.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Harami bin Ammarah told us: Shu’bah told us: Ammarah told me on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
And leave the sea at ease
, he said: Gentle.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease
, he said: Easy and pleasant.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease
, he said: It is the plain.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Leave it dry and new.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ubaidullah bin Muadh told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And leave the sea at ease
, he said: Fresh.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ubayd God ibn Muadh told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And leave the sea at rest
, he said: Dry, as it was after you struck it. He said: Do not order it to return, leave it until the last of them enters.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: a path of ease, he said: a dry path.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And leave the sea as a path, as it is, a dry road. The most correct of the sayings about this is the one that says that its meaning is: Leave it as it was when you took it. This is because in the speech of the Arabs, raho means stillness, as the poet said: As if the people of Hajar were watching when they saw me outside, a singing bird.
h
And leave the sea at rest
. Indeed,
h
they are a drowned army

. A bird saw a hawk dripping with blood, and its mother went out to Eid That is, at rest. If that is what it means, then there is no doubt that it was left easy and smooth, and a dry path, because the Children of Israel crossed it when they crossed it, and it was like that. So if the sea was left calm as it was when Moses crossed it, calm and not agitated, then there is no doubt that it was in the manner described. His saying:
h
They are a drowned army
means: Pharaoh and his people are God’s army who will be drowned in the sea.

x: God Almighty says: How many gardens and trees did Pharaoh and his people leave behind among the Copts after their destruction and God drowning them, and springs, meaning: and sources of what used to gush forth in their gardens and crops standing in their farms.
And a noble position He says: And a noble and noble position they used to occupy. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of God’s description of that station as generous.
Some of them said: He described it thus because of its honor, and that is because it is the station of kings and princes. They said: What is meant by it is the pulpits.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Jaafar Ibn Bint Ishaq Al-Azraq told me, he said: Saeed Ibn Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told us, he said: Ismail Ibn Ibrahim Ibn Muhajir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a noble station
, he said: The pulpits.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Abdullah bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a noble station
, he said: The pulpits.

x: Others said: He described that place as generous because of its beauty and splendor.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And a noble station
means: good.

x: And His statement:
h
And they were brought out of a blessing in which they were enjoying themselves
. God Almighty says:
h
And they were brought out of a blessing in which they were enjoying themselves

, reveling in it, and enjoying it. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase fakihin. Most of the regions except Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ read it fakihin with the meaning I described. Abu Rajaʿ al-ʿAttardi, al-Hasan, and Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani read it fakihin meaning: arrogant and haughty. The correct reading in my opinion is the reading used by the readers of the regions, which is fakihin with an alif, meaning soft. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they were enjoying pleasure in it: comfortable. He said: Yes, by God, God expelled him from his gardens, his springs, and his crops until He threw him into the sea.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase fakihin.
Most of the regions except Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ read it fakihin with the meaning I described.
Abu Rajaʿ al-ʿAttardi, al-Hasan, and Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani read it fakihin meaning: arrogant and haughty.
The correct reading in my opinion is the reading used by the readers of the regions, which is fakihin with an alif, meaning soft.

x: And His statement: Likewise, We caused another people to inherit it. God Almighty says: Thus, as I have described to you, O people, We did with those whose affair I have mentioned to you, who denied Our Messenger Moses, peace and blessings be upon him. And His statement:
h
And We caused another people to inherit it

, God Almighty says: And We caused their gardens, springs, crops, dwellings, and whatever blessings they had enjoyed to be inherited from them to another people after their destruction. It was said that what is meant by the other people are the Children of Israel.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Likewise,
h
and We caused another people to inherit it
, meaning the Children of Israel.

x: God Almighty says: So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for those whom God drowned in the sea, namely Pharaoh and his people. It has been said that the weeping of the heavens is the redness of its edges.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told me, he said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hammad told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Zuhair, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When Al-Hussein bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, was killed, the sky wept for him, and its weeping was its redness.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them

, he said: Its weeping is the redness of its edges. It was said: The heavens and the earth did not weep for them is because when a believer dies, the heavens and the earth weep for him for forty mornings, but they did not weep for Pharaoh and his people, because they had no good deeds that would ascend to God, so the heavens would weep for them, nor any mosque on earth, so the earth would weep for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Those who said that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying:

c: Talq bin Ghanam narrated to us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: O Abu Abbas, tell me about the statement of God, the Most High: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. Do the heavens and the earth weep for anyone? He said: Yes, there is no one among creation but that he has a door in the heaven from which his provision descends and through which his deeds ascend. So when a believer dies and his door in the heaven through which his deeds ascended and his provision descended is closed, he is wept for. And when his place of prayer is lost in the land in which he used to pray and remember God, he is wept for. The people of Pharaoh had no good traces on the earth, and no good ascended from them to the heaven. He said: So the heavens and the earth did not weep for them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman and Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: It was said: The earth weeps over the believer for forty mornings.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Yahya bin Talha told me: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: I was told that when a believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami told us: Bakir ibn Abi al-Sumait told us: Qatada told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: that he used to say: The regions of the earth from which his deeds ascend to the heavens weep for him after his death, meaning the believer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them. He said: There is no one but that he has a door in the heaven through which his provision descends and through which his deeds ascend. Then, when he loses it, the places where he used to prostrate weep for him. And the people of Pharaoh did not have any righteous deeds on earth that would be accepted from them, so that they would ascend to God Almighty. So Mujahid said: The earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: It was said: When a believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings. Yahya bin Talha narrated:

c: Isa bin Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubaid Al-Hadrami, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange. There is no strangeness for the believer. No believer dies in a foreign land in which his mourners are absent from him, but the heavens and the earth weep for him.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them,’ then he said: ‘They do not weep for the disbeliever.’”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them… the verse
. He said: That is because there is no believer on earth who dies except that the mosques in which he used to pray weep for him when they lose him, and except that the place in heaven from which

x: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment: God Almighty says: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the punishment with which Pharaoh and his people were tormenting them. Humiliating means humiliating them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment by killing their sons and keeping their women alive.

x: And His statement: "From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors." God the Almighty says: And We had certainly saved the Children of Israel from the punishment from Pharaoh. So His statement:
h
From Pharaoh is a repetition of His statement

: From the humiliating punishment, a substitution of the first. What is meant by His statement: Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors is that he was a tyrant, haughty and arrogant towards his Lord. Of the transgressors means: of those who transgressed beyond what they should not transgress. Rather, God the Almighty means that he was aggressive in his disbelief and arrogant towards his Lord the Almighty.

God Almighty says: And We chose the Children of Israel, with knowledge from Us, over the people of their time at that time, and that was the time of Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds
: meaning they were chosen over the people of their time, and every time has a scholar.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds
, he said: The world of that time.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds
, he said: over those who were among them.

x: His statement: And We gave them signs in which there was a clear trial. God Almighty says: And We gave them lessons and morals in which there was a test, which makes clear to whoever contemplates it that it was a test with which God tested them.
The interpreters differed regarding this affliction.
Some of them said: He afflicted them with His blessings upon them.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: And We gave them signs in which there was clear trial means that God saved them from their enemy, then He cut off the sea for them, shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails.

x: Others said: Rather, He tested them with ease and hardship.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We gave them of the signs that which was a clear trial, and he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned.
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 35)

and he said: A clear trial for whoever believed in it and disbelieved in it, a trial with which We test them, We purify them with a trial of testing, We test them with good and evil, We test them to see from what He gave them of the signs who will believe in it, benefit from it and waste it. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God informed us that He gave the Children of Israel signs that would test and try them. The test and trial may be in ease or in hardship, and He did not provide us with evidence from the report or reason that He meant some of that and not others. God tested them with both meanings together. It is possible that He meant that He tested them with both of them. If the matter is as we have described, then the correct thing to say about it is as God, the Most High, said that He tested them.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what the polytheists of Quraysh said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: These polytheists from your people, O Muhammad, say, ‘It is only our first death,’ which we will die, and it is the first death.

And we will not be resurrected after our death, nor will we be sent forth, as a denial from them of resurrection, reward, and punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Indeed, these people say: ‘There is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected.’” He said: The polytheists of the Arabs said: And we will not be resurrected, meaning: they will not be resurrected.

x: And His statement:
h
Then bring our fathers
, if you should be truthful. God Almighty says: They said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:
h
Then bring our fathers

who have died, if you should be truthful, that God will raise us up after our trial in our graves, and revive us after our death. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was addressed, and he alone is addressed to everyone, as it was said: O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1) and as He said: My Lord, send me back (al-Mu’minun 23:99). And I have explained that in more than one place in our book.
God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Are these polytheists, O Muhammad, better than your people, or the people of Tubba’, meaning Tubba’ al-Himyari?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Are they better or the people of Tubba’? He said: The Himyarites.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Are they better, the people of Tubba’? He told us that the people of Tubba’ were a man from Himyar, he marched with armies until he bewildered Al-Hirah, then he came to Samarkand and destroyed it. He told us that if he wrote in the name of the one he called himself and ruled over land and sea, health and wind. He told us that Ka’b used to say: Describe the description of the righteous man, God will blame his people with a blame that he blames him. Aisha used to say: Do not curse Tubba’, for he was a righteous man.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Aisha said:
m: Tubba' was a righteous man. Ka'b said: God condemned his people, but He did not condemn him.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Tamim ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: that Tubba’ covered the Kaaba. Sa’id forbade cursing it. And His statement:
h
And those before them means that God Almighty says

: Are these polytheists from Quraysh better or the people of Tubba and those before them from the nations who disbelieved in their Lord? He says: These are not better than those, so we should pardon them and not destroy them, and they are disbelievers in God, just as those nations before them whom We destroyed were disbelievers. His statement: Indeed, they were criminals means: The people of Tubba’ and those before them of the nations whom We destroyed, We only destroyed them because of their crimes and their disbelief in their Lord. It was said: They were criminals, so the alif of in was broken as a starting point, and it has the meaning of a condition, as the speech does not indicate its meaning.

x: God Almighty says: And We did not create the seven heavens and the earths and everything between them in play.

And His statement: We did not create them except with the truth means: We did not create the heavens and the earth except with the truth without which management is not valid. And by that, the Most High means to point out the truth of resurrection and recompense. The Most High says: We did not create the creation in vain, by bringing them to life as We willed, then annihilating them without testing them with obedience, commands and prohibitions, and without rewarding the obedient for his obedience, and the disobedient for his disobedience. Rather, We created this to test whomever We willed to test from among Our creation with whatever test We willed of commands and prohibitions. That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness. (al-Najm 53:31) But most of them do not know. God Almighty says: But most of these polytheists do not know that God created for them, so they do not fear God’s wrath as punishment for what they do, nor do they expect any good reward for what they do, because of their denial of the afterlife.

God Almighty says: The Day God will judge between His creation for what they did in this world of good or evil, He will reward the doer of good with good, and the doer of evil with evil. A time for them all together: He says: A time for their gathering all together.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all is the day on which people will be judged by their deeds.

x: And His statement: On the Day when no protector will avail another protector at all, meaning: no cousin will ward off another cousin, nor a friend from his friend, from anything of the punishment that has befallen them from God. Nor will they be aided, meaning: nor will they aid one another, so they seek refuge from whoever has afflicted them with punishment, as they used to do in this world.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: On the Day when no protector will avail another at all… the verse, on that Day, O son of Adam, all causes will be cut off, and people will return to their deeds. So whoever attains good on that Day will be happy with it as a final consequence of his deeds, and whoever attains evil on that Day will be miserable with it as a final consequence of his deeds.

x: And his statement:
h
Except for whom God has mercy The Arab scholars differed regarding the position of <of>in his statement
h
Except for whom God has mercy
, so some of the grammarians of Basra said:
h
Except for whom God has mercy
, so he made it a substitute for the implied noun in they will be helped, and if you wish you can make it the subject and implied its predicate, meaning:
h
Except for whom God has mercy
, so it will suffice. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement:
h
Except for whom God has mercy

, he said: The believers intercede for one another, so if you wish you can make <of>in the nominative case, as if you said: No one can stand except so-and-so, and if you wish you can make it the accusative as an exception and a break from the beginning of the sentence, meaning: O God,
h
except for whom God has mercy

Others among them said: Its meaning is: A master cannot avail another master at all, except for someone whom God has given permission to intercede. He said: It cannot be a substitute for what is in they will be helped, because except is definite, the first is negated, and a substitute can only have the meaning of the first. He said: Likewise, it is not permissible for it to be a new sentence, because it cannot be a new sentence with an exception. The most correct of the sayings about this is that it is in the nominative case, meaning: On the Day when no protector will avail another protector at all, except for those upon whom God has mercy, for He will avail him by interceding for him with his Lord. And His saying: Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. God Almighty says, describing Himself: Indeed, God is the Exalted in His vengeance against His enemies, the Merciful to His friends and those who obey Him.

God the Most High says: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum which He informed us grows at the bottom of Hell, which He made food for the people of Hell, its fruit in Hell is the food of the sinner in this world with regard to his Lord. The sinner is the one who commits sin, and sin comes from athama to sin, meaning to be sinful, so he is athim atheem. What is meant by it here is the one whose sin is disbelief in his Lord, not any other sin.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam bin al-Harith,
m: that Abu al-Darda’ was teaching a man, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is food for the sinner, and he said, Food for the orphan, so Abu al-Darda’ said, Say, ‘Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is food for the wicked.’

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If a drop of the Zaqqum of Hell were sent down to the world, it would ruin people’s livelihood.

c: Abu al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, who said:
m: Abu al-Darda’ was teaching a man, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful. The man kept saying, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the orphan. When Abu al-Darda’ continued to repeat this verse, he saw that he did not understand, so he said, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful, he said: Abu Jahl.

x: And His statement:
h
Like boiling molten metal in the bellies

, God Almighty says: The tree of Zaqqum, whose fruit is made the food of the disbeliever in Hell, is like lead or silver, or what is melted in fire when it is melted in it, so its heat is extreme, and its rage is intense in the intense blackness. We have previously explained the meaning of the term period of grace in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here in this context, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among the scholars of interpretation regarding it. However, we will mention from the statements of the scholars in this context what we did not mention there.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, the Most High, like molten copper. He said: Like the dregs of oil.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like boiling oil in the bellies
, meaning: black like boiling oil. Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa’ib, and Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us:

c: Ibn Idris told us:
m: I heard Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: like molten metal: thick water like the dregs of oil.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abd Al-Samad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he saw silver that had been melted, and he said: This is the molten metal.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, he said: Amr bin Maymun told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Like molten copper that scorcheth faces (al-Kahf 18

:29), he said: Abdullah entered the treasury, and brought out some remains that were in it, and lit a fire over them until they sparkled. He said: Where is the one who asked about the molten copper? This is the molten copper. Ibn Bashar narrated: Ibn Abi Uday narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated: Awf narrated: al-Hasan narrated: It reached me that Ibn Masʿud was asked about the molten metal which they say on the Day of Resurrection is the drink of the people of Hell, and which is under the control of the public treasury. He said: So he called for gold and silver and melted them and said: This is the most similar thing in this world to the molten metal which is the color of the sky on the Day of Resurrection and the drink of the people of Hell, except that it is hotter than this. The wording of the hadith is from Ibn Bashar, and the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna is similar.

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Ash’ath told us, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: Among his words was that Abdullah ibn Mas’ud was a man whom God had honoured by allowing him to be a companion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar, may God be pleased with him, appointed him over the treasury. He said: So he took a large amount of broken silver and dug a trench for it. Then he ordered a large amount of firewood to be brought and lit a fire over it. When it bubbled and foamed and changed into various colours, he said: Look who is at the door. So he brought the people in and said to them: This is the most similar thing we have ever seen in the world to molten metal.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * Is food for the sinful… the verse. It was mentioned to us that Ibn Masoud was given a gift of a water trough made of gold and silver, so he ordered that a trench be dug in the ground, then large pieces of firewood were thrown into it, then that water trough was thrown into it, until it foamed and dissolved. He said to his servant: Call whoever is present with us from the people of Kufa. So he called a group, and when they entered he said: Do you see this? They said: Yes. He said: We have not seen in the world anything similar to molten metal closer than this gold and silver when it foams and dissolves.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sufyan Al-Asadi, who said:
m: Abdullah bin Masoud melted silver, then said: Whoever wants to look at the molten metal, let him look at this.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day when the sky will be like molten copper (al-Ma’arij 70
:8), he said: Like the dregs of oil.

c: Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: Like the dregs of oil. He said: Like the dregs of oil.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yaʿmar bin Bishr told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us: Abu Al-Sabah told us:
m: I heard Yazid bin Abi Sumayyah say: I heard Ibn Umar say: Do you know what Mahl is? Mahl is the end of the oil, meaning its end.

x: Boils means: the food of the sinner boils, or the boiling pot boils.
Some of them mentioned it to remind people of the food, and they interpreted its meaning to mean that the food is what boils in their stomachs.

Some of them mentioned it to remind people of the boiling pot, and they interpreted it to mean that it is an attribute of the boiling pot. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. Like the boiling of scalding water means: It boils in the bellies of these wretched people like the boiling of scalding water, which is heated water that has been lit until it reaches the peak of its heat. It was also said to be scalding water and it is scalding, because it is changed from maf’ul to fa’il, just as it is said qatil, from maqtul.

The Almighty says: Take him, meaning this sinner with his Lord, about whom the Most High has informed us that the tree of Zaqqum is food. Then ascend him, the Almighty says: Push him and drive him. It is said from this: Atala ya’talahu ‘atlan: if he drives him by pushing and pulling. From this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: The generous are not like your father until you return to Atiya It is pushed and pulled. His statement, to the middle of Hellfire, means to the middle of Hellfire. The meaning of the statement is that it will be said on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Take this sinner and drive him, pushing him on his back and dragging him to the middle of the Fire. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: So they climbed on him, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Take him and throw him into the midst of Hellfire

, he said: Take him and push him. In his saying: So they ascended it, there are two pronunciations: breaking the ta, which is the reading of some of the people of Medina and some of the people of Mecca. The correct reading of this, according to us, is that they are two dialects in Arabic, and it is said: ‘Atal, Ya’tal, and Ya’tal. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: To the middle of Hellfire means to the middle of the fire.

evidence.text: In his saying: So they ascended it, there are two pronunciations: breaking the ta, which is the reading of some of the people of Medina and some of the people of Mecca.
The correct reading of this, according to us, is that they are two dialects in Arabic, and it is said: ‘Atal, Ya’tal, and Ya’tal.

x: And His statement:
h
Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water

. God Almighty says: Then they poured over this sinner’s head the torment of scalding water, meaning: the heated water whose description we have described, and which is the water about which God said, With it will melt what is in their bellies and their skins, and its description has been explained there.

God Almighty says: It will be said to this sinful, wretched person: Taste this torment with which you are being tormented today. Indeed, you are the honorable one among your people, the generous one over them. He mentioned that these verses were revealed about Abu Jahl bin Hisham.
Those who said that: Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water. This was revealed about the enemy of God, Abu Jahl. “He met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he seized him and shook him, then he said: ‘It is more fitting for you, O Abu Jahl, then it is more fitting for you, then it is more fitting for you. Taste that you are the mighty and noble.’ That is because he said: ‘Does Muhammad promise me? By God, I am more mighty than anyone who walked between two mountains.” This is also the case with And do not obey any sinner or ungrateful among them. (al-Insan 76:24), and this is also the case with No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near. (al-Alaq 96:19) Qatada said: This was revealed about Abu Jahl and his companions whom God, the Blessed and Exalted, killed on the day of Badr. Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction?
r
(Ibrahim 14:28)

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Seize him and ascend him was revealed about Abu Jahl. Qatada said: Abu Jahl said: There is no man between the two mountains more honorable or more generous than me. So God Almighty said: Taste, for you are the honorable, the generous.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Take him and throw him into the midst of Hellfire, he said: This is for Abu Jahl.

x: How could it be said, while he is being humiliated with the torment mentioned by God, and is being humbled by violence to the level of Hellfire:
h
You are the Exalted
, the Generous?
His saying:
h
You are the Exalted

, the Generous is not a description of the one who said that to him with honor and generosity, but rather it is an appreciation from him for what he used to describe himself with in this world, and a rebuke to him with that in the form of a narrative, because in this world he used to say:
h
You are the Exalted

, the Generous, so it would be said to him in the Hereafter, when he is tormented with what he was tormented with in the Fire: “Taste this humiliation today, for you used to claim that you were the Exalted, the Generous, and that you were the one who was humiliated and degraded. So where is that which you used to say and claim of honor and generosity? Why do you not protect yourself from the torment with your honor?”

Ibn Bashar narrated: Sufyan ibn Isa narrated: Ibn Ajlan narrated from Saeed Al-Maqburi from Abu Hurairah who said: Kaab said: God has three garments: He wraps Himself in glory, He dresses Himself in mercy, and He wears the garment of majesty. Exalted is He. Whoever is proud of something other than that which God has honored him with, he is the one for whom it is said: Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. Whoever is merciful to people, he is the one for whom God has clothed himself in the garment that befits him. Whoever is arrogant, he is the one who has disputed with God over His cloak. God, the Exalted, says: It is not fitting for one who disputes with Me over My cloak that I should admit him to Paradise. The Qur’an reciters of all regions unanimously agreed to pronounce the alif in the phrase Think, for you with a kasra as a starting point. And the account of the saying of this speaker: I am the mighty, the generous.

Some of the later scholars read it as Think, for you with a fatha on the alif, based on the word Think in the phrase for you, as if the meaning of the statement to him was: Taste this statement that you said in this world. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is to break the alif of inka according to the meaning that I mentioned to its reader, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and the anomaly of what contradicts it. And sufficient evidence of the error of a reading contrary to it is what the imams of the past and present have followed, despite its distance from correctness in meaning and its separation from the interpretation of the people of interpretation.

evidence.text: The Qur’an reciters of all regions unanimously agreed to pronounce the alif in the phrase Think, for you with a kasra as a starting point.

Some of the later scholars read it as Think, for you with a fatha on the alif, based on the word Think in the phrase for you, as if the meaning of the statement to him was: Taste this statement that you said in this world.

The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is to break the alif of inka according to the meaning that I mentioned to its reader, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and the anomaly of what contradicts it.

And sufficient evidence of the error of a reading contrary to it is what the imams of the past and present have followed, despite its distance from correctness in meaning and its separation from the interpretation of the people of interpretation.

x: And His statement:
h
This is what you were in doubt about

, God Almighty says: It will be said to him: This torment with which you are being tormented today is the torment about which you were in doubt in this world, and about which you disputed, and about which you were not certain. You have encountered it, so taste it.

God Almighty says: Indeed, those who fear Him by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience in a place of residence, are safe in that place from what they feared in the stations of this world of afflictions, illnesses, calamities, and sorrows. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase: in the place of a trustworthy person. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as in the place of a trustworthy person with a damma on the meem, meaning: in the residence of a trustworthy person during the journey. The majority of the reciters of Egypt, Kufa and Basra, read it as in a place with a fatha on the meem, with the meaning we have described, and indicating that they are in the place and position of a trustworthy person. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions, and their meanings are correct. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position Yes, by God, secure from Satan, idols, and sorrows.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase: in the place of a trustworthy person.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as in the place of a trustworthy person with a damma on the meem, meaning: in the residence of a trustworthy person during the journey.

The majority of the reciters of Egypt, Kufa and Basra, read it as in a place with a fatha on the meem, with the meaning we have described, and indicating that they are in the place and position of a trustworthy person.
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions, and their meanings are correct.

x: And his saying:
h
In gardens and springs

. The gardens and springs are a translation of the secure station, and the secure station is the gardens and springs, and the gardens are the orchards, and the springs are the springs of water flowing continuously at the roots of the trees of the gardens.
And His statement:
h
They will wear fine silk
, meaning: These righteous people will wear fine silk in these gardens, which is the finest type of brocade, and heavy brocade, which is the thickest type of brocade.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: Of fine silk and heavy brocade, he said: Heavy brocade is thick silk. It was said:
h
They will wear fine silk
and brocade, and he did not say clothing, as the meaning of the words is sufficient. His saying:
h
Facing each other means that in Paradise they will face each other
, and they will not look at each other’s backs. We have mentioned the narration about that previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

x: God Almighty says: Just as We have given these righteous people honor in the Hereafter by admitting them into the Gardens and dressing them therein in fine silk and brocade, likewise We have honored them by also marrying them therein to houris from among the women, who are pure white, and their singular is: houri.
Mujahid used to say about the meaning of the houris:

c: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, and Al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa’ both narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And We shall marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes, he said: We married them to fair women. He said: The fair women are those whom the eye is dazzled by, the marrow of their shins is visible from behind their clothes, and the observer sees his face in the liver of one of them like a mirror because of the thinness of their skin and the purity of their complexion. What Mujahid said, that the meaning of fair women is that which the eye is dazzled by, is a statement that has no meaning in Arabic speech, because fair women is the plural of houri, just as humr is the plural of hamra’, and as-sawd is the plural of sawda’, and hawra’ is a verbal noun from hawra, which means pure whiteness, just as the pure whiteness of food is called hawari. We have explained the meaning of that with supporting evidence previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Thus, We will marry them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes. He said: White, beautiful eyes. He said: And in Ibn Masoud’s reading: with fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: Hoor with wide eyes, he said: White with wide eyes. He said: And in the version of Ibn Mas’ud: Ba’ees with wide eyes. Ibn Mas’ud recited this, meaning that the meaning of Hoor is not the one that Mujahid went with, because Ays among the Arabs is the plural of Aysa, which is the white camel, as al-A’sha said: The mission of a displaced person, the wolves howl at him, cost Aais a cawing under the man By A’is he means: a white camel. As for Ain, it is the plural of Aynaa, which is a woman with large eyes.

evidence.text: Ibn Mas’ud recited this, meaning that the meaning of Hoor is not the one that Mujahid went with, because Ays among the Arabs is the plural of Aysa, which is the white camel, as al-A’sha said: The mission of a displaced person, the wolves howl at him, cost Aais a cawing under the man By A’is he means: a white camel.

x: And His statement,
h
They will call therein

... the verse, means: These righteous people will call therein for every type of fruit of Paradise that they desire, safe therein from its being cut off from them, running out, or vanishing, and from the harm and evil that it causes. He means: That fruit there is not like the fruit of this world that we eat, and they fear the evil consequences of it, and the aftermath of its harm, even though it will run out from them, and become non-existent at some times and periods.
Qatada directed the interpretation of his saying: safe to what:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They will call therein
for every kind of fruit, safe and sound. They will be safe from death, illness, and Satan.

x: And His statement:
h
They will not taste death therein except the first death

. God Almighty says: These righteous people will not taste death in Paradise after the first death that they tasted in this world. Some Arab scholars interpreted the word except in this context to mean except and said: The meaning of the statement is:
h
They will not taste death therein except the first death
. He gives an example of this with the words of God Almighty: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred
r
(An-Nisa’: 22)

, meaning: except what your fathers have done. What he said has no clear basis in my opinion, because what is most likely when someone says: I will not taste food today except the food I tasted before today is that he means to inform the speaker that he has food on that day that he will taste and eat, unlike all other foods. If this is the most likely meaning, then it must have been proven by his words:
h
Except the first death that it is a death of the same type as the first death
, which they will taste.

It is known that this is not the case, because God Almighty has made the people of Paradise safe in Paradise if they enter it from death, but its meaning is as I have described. It is permissible to put <except>in place of <after>because their meanings are close in this context. That is because if a speaker says: I will not speak to a man today except a man with Amr, he has obligated himself not to speak to a man that day after speaking to the man with Amr. Likewise, if he says: I will not speak to a man today after a man with Amr, he has obligated himself not to speak to a man that day except a man with Amr. So after and except are close in meaning in this context. It is the custom of the Arabs to put one word in place of another if their meanings are close, like putting hope in place of fear because of the fear in the meaning of hope, because hope is not certainty, but rather greed, and it may be true or false, just as fear sometimes comes true and sometimes lies.

i: So, in this regard, Aw Dhu’ayb said:
x: If a wasp stings him, he will not be stung by it, and he will oppose it in the house of Nubb factors He said: He did not fear its sting, meaning: He did not fear its sting. And they put suspicion in place of knowledge that was not perceived by sight, but was perceived by inference or report, as the poet said: I told them that they thought that two thousand armed men were their leaders in the Persian armor.

Meaning: Be certain of two thousand armed men and know. So assumption was put in place of certainty if those to whom that was said had not witnessed two thousand armed men, nor seen them, and what this informant had informed them of, so he said to them, assume knowledge of what has not been witnessed is an action of the heart. So one was put in place of the other because their meanings are close in similarities to what I have mentioned, the enumeration of which is great. Just as the meanings of the two words are close in some meanings. They have different meanings in other things, so the Arabs place one of them in place of the other in the place where their meanings are close. Likewise, His statement,
h
They will not taste death therein except the first death

, He placed except in place of after because we describe the closeness of the meaning of except and after in this place. Likewise, And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred
r
(An-Nisa’: 22)
, its meaning is: after what occurred from you in the pre-Islamic period.

But if except is directed in this place to the meaning of except, then it is a translation of the place, and an explanation of it with what is more confusing for whoever wants to know its meaning from it.

And His statement: And He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire, as a favor from your Lord. God Almighty says: And these righteous people will be protected by their Lord on that Day from the punishment of Hellfire, as a favor from your Lord, O Muhammad, and as a kindness from Him to them thereby. He will not punish them for a crime they committed in the past in this world. And were it not for His favor to them by pardoning them for their past punishment, He would not have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire, but its pain and distress would have reached them and afflicted them. And His statement:
h
That is the great attainment

. God Almighty says: This which We have given to these righteous people in the Hereafter of honor that is described in these verses, is the great attainment. He says: It is the great victory in what they sought to attain in this world through their deeds and obedience to their Lord, and their fear of Him, in what He tested them with of acts of obedience and obligations, and avoidance of forbidden things.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have only made easy the recitation of this Qur’an which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, in your language, so that these polytheists to whom We have sent you may remember its lessons and arguments, and be admonished by its sermons, and reflect on its verses when you recite it to them, so that they may return to the obedience of their Lord, and submit to the truth when it becomes clear to them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
We have only made it easy in your language
: meaning this Qur’an that they may remember.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: We have only made it easy for your tongue, he said: the Qur’an, and We made it easy: He set his tongue at ease with it.

evidence.text: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have only made easy the recitation of this Qur’an which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, in your language, so that these polytheists to whom We have sent you may remember its lessons and arguments, and be admonished by its sermons, and reflect on its verses when you recite it to them, so that they may return to the obedience of their Lord, and submit to the truth when it becomes clear to them.

x: And His saying: So wait, for they are waiting. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So wait, O Muhammad, for the victory from your Lord, and the victory over these polytheists among your people from Quraysh, for they are waiting in their hearts for your subjugation and your dominance by turning away from the truth that you have brought them, whoever wants to accept it and follow you in it. And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: Then wait, for they are waiting, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then wait, for they are waiting. That is, wait, for they are waiting.

x: Commentary on Sūrat Smoke (al-Dukhān). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 210 عن معمر به، وهو في تفسير سفيان ص 283 قال: في قراءة عبد الله. فذكره، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 33 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported it in his Tafsīr, as cited in Taghlīq al-Taʿlīq (4/310–311), through Shaybān, from Qatādah. The original adds: ‘The forty-fourth part is complete, and all praise is due to God as He deserves; next, God willing, is the interpretation of Sūrat al-Jāthiyah.’ This concludes the forty-fourth part. The reader will find the T1 manuscript folio numbers in square brackets.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد بن حميد في تفسيره - كما في تعليق التعليق 4/ 310، 311 - من طريق شيبان، عن قتادة. وبعده في الأصل: "تم السفر والحمد لله حق حمده، يتلوه إن شاء الله تفسير سورة الجاثية". وبه ينتهى الجزء الرابع والأربعون، وسيجد القارئ أرقام النسخة ت 1 بين معكوفين.
